purpose: The 4-row dry run section 6.6 of docs/readiness/2026-09-06-e22-dev-usage-cells-v1-preregistration.md requires before cell (b) flies, on four rows of the same 1,500-row roster chosen before any contact to bracket it (longest, shortest, median, p90 by duration). Three reads, in order of importance: (1) does the per-sample cap actually reach the wire as four DIFFERENT integers -- 3, 55, 127 and 321 -- and does each equal the rule's own resolution for that row's duration, read back out of the sealed trace's decoding_params; (2) do both ESB scorers resolve references from the dev10 hash-pinned layer and score the sealed manifest through core.scoring_batch with verified = true; (3) a wall-time reading for the flight's projection. The smoke's own WER numbers are on four rows and enter no verdict.

E22-ESB-DEV1500-SMOKE-4.selection: deterministic and pre-registered, the same rule the 2026-09-05 dev smoke used: the longest utterance (the window-fit and VRAM worst case), the shortest, the median and the p90 by duration over the drawn 1,500, ties broken by sample id

cells.serving_geometry: -c 40960 -np 8, 5120 tokens per slot -- identical to the flight
cells.factor: none; this is cell (b)'s own protocol on four rows

shared_protocol.audio_path: raw audio, bf16 mmproj resident on the GPU, no feature cache directory
shared_protocol.max_tokens: PER SAMPLE, the same rule the flight sends
shared_protocol.obs: none -- an ESB utterance IS the request

evaluation.paper_facing_aggregation: corpus: total S+D+I over total reference words
metrics: the per-row resolved max_tokens read back out of the sealed trace's decoding_params, against the rule's own resolution for that row's duration
completion tokens per row against that row's cap -- whether the cap bound at all on four rows
latency, throughput, peak VRAM and any CUDA fault or out-of-memory
whether both ESB scorers returned per-sample rows through core.scoring_batch with verified = true

execution_plan_basis.planned_model_calls: 4 rows x 1 contact = 4, plus headroom for a canary and one recovery attempt; the registered ceiling is 60. core/model/adapter.py meters the plan cumulatively across every attempt of this run id.
execution_plan_basis.planned_speech_audio_seconds: 51.7005 s for one pass, rounded up to 120 to cover a recovery attempt; the registered ceiling is 200.
execution_plan_basis.planned_gpu_hours: 0.25, essentially all of it model load; the registered ceiling is 0.5.

decision.go_no_go: The flight launches only if all four reads are affirmative: the four requests carried four DIFFERENT resolved integers and each equals the rule's own resolution for that row's duration; the -c 40960 -np 8 geometry serves without an out-of-memory or CUDA fault; both ESB scorers return per-sample rows on the sealed manifest through core.scoring_batch with verified = true; and the projected flight time is at or under the registered ceiling.
decision.claim_surface: none; a smoke's numbers enter no verdict
